name: NJ-08
label: Safe D

key_factors: No Republican on the ballot; three underfunded independents are the only opposition
Strong Democratic district (D+15) with a favorable environment for the incumbent's party
Menendez's commanding financial position: about $2M raised, $680K on hand, plus outside support
Prediction markets price a Democratic hold near 95%
model.rationale: The absence of a major-party nominee, a fifteen-point Democratic district, and the incumbent's large fundraising edge leave only nominal opposition, and markets agree the seat stays Democratic by a wide margin.
model.watch: A late fundraising surge or unexpected traction for Eliopoulos, or an unforeseen scandal involving the incumbent, would be the main ways this tightens.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Aristotle Eliopoulos is an independent standing in for the Republican side.

overview:
Rob Menendez, the Democratic incumbent, enters the general election after securing renomination in a district that leans Democratic by fifteen points. No Republican filed to run; the opposition consists of three independents led by Aristotle Eliopoulos, none of whom report meaningful fundraising. Menendez has raised roughly two million dollars, holds about seven hundred thousand on hand, and benefits from outside spending on his behalf.

With no party-backed challenger and no public polling in the race, the structural picture dominates: the seat's strong Democratic tilt, the incumbent's financial advantage, and prediction markets pricing a Democratic win around ninety-five percent all point the same way. The realistic uncertainty concerns the size of the victory margin rather than the winner, though the lack of polling keeps that estimate loose.
